common_name: William Shakespeare Rose (Original 1987 David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or grafted plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air movement and fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost.

directions: Introduced by David Austin in 1987, William Shakespeare bears deeply cupped, very full, velvety crimson-purple blooms that darken toward wine-purple with age, carrying a strong old-rose fragrance on a vigorous, somewhat arching shrub. It proved notably prone to blackspot and mildew in humid climates, which prompted Austin to introduce the sturdier, similarly colored William Shakespeare 2000 as a replacement roughly a decade later, though the original is still occasionally sought by collectors for its especially saturated color and heavy fragrance. Keep air moving freely around the canes and maintain a proactive fungicide program in humid regions to limit disease pressure. Prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood, and deadhead through the season to sustain repeat bloom.
